purpose: Bounded interface-correction diagnostic after the new contextual-code flow omitted the terminal per-residue layer normalization used by the inherited latent samplers. Keep the failed unprojected recipe and outputs unchanged. No retraining, checkpoint, solver-step, strength or threshold sweep.
diagnosis: All1392 native training context labels have residue mean zero and norm sqrt8 to float32 precision. Unprojected isolated samples have residue standard deviation0.863to1.077 and maximum absolute residue mean0.03483. Global channel statistics concealed this violation. The existing scaffold sampler normalizes its terminal output but repeatedly sees unnormalized clamped motif targets during RePaint. This is an interface mismatch; whether it explains failure is untested.
correction: Apply torch.nn.functional.layer_norm(codes,(8,)) with default epsilon1e-5 once after channel unnormalization and before using codes as RePaint targets. Never rotate8-channel codes or average samples. Reject nonfinite or degenerate input variance. Keep original20codes, output projections and all provenance arrays separately.

Additionally normalize the same native oracle motif codes and require unchanged16raw/valid decisions plus backbone CA RMSD<=.2A,lDDT>=.99.
